rules.heading: State claims (tail of the rule opening before line 751)
rules.quote: is in is read in the same turn and said from the read. Otherwise the sentence says "I think"
rules.says: A sentence stating what state a build, release, CI, pipeline, worktree, working copy or remote is in must be read in the same turn and said from that read; otherwise the sentence says "I think" and the reply offers the check.
rules.live_quote: - A statement of state is read in the same turn, never remembered.
rules.missing: That otherwise the sentence says "I think" and the reply offers the check; also the list of what counts as state (task, agent, branch, push, deploy, file, workflow, run, commit, build, release, CI, pipeline, worktree, remote).

rules.heading: State claims (tail of the rule opening before line 751)
rules.quote: or, when checking would be a big job, the question goes to the owner first.
rules.says: When checking a state claim would be a big job, the question goes to the owner first instead of the session running the check.

rules.heading: State claims (tail of the rule opening before line 751)
rules.quote: *Enforced by:* `stop-guard.mjs`. A reply saying what state one of those is in is refused when no tool result came back in that turn
rules.says: A reply saying what state one of those things is in is refused when no tool result came back in that turn, and it passes only when the sentence says "I think" and the reply asks whether to run the check.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The gates live in the hub and run however a session is launched.** A session's first plan clones the hub to `/root/.claude/hub` and installs
rules.says: The gates live in the hub and run however a session is launched: a session's first plan clones the hub to /root/.claude/hub and installs hook-dispatch.mjs from that clone, and gates installed inside an approved plan go live mid-session with no restart.
rules.missing: That a session's first plan clones the hub, and that gates installed inside an approved plan go live mid-session with no restart (live installs by environment setup script instead).

rules.heading: (plan rules, after rule 15)
rules.quote: **A paragraph a gate enforces whole is replaced by one line naming the gate.** The doctrine is read in full at every startup
rules.says: When a gate enforces a doctrine paragraph whole, that paragraph is replaced by one line reading `*Enforced whole by:*` and the gate's file name in backticks, with what it said and why staying in the lesson that recorded it.

rules.heading: (plan rules, after rule 15)
rules.quote: A paragraph a gate enforces only in part stays, and says which part.
rules.says: A paragraph that a gate enforces only in part is kept in the doctrine and must say which part the gate enforces.

rules.heading: (plan rules, after rule 15)
rules.quote: Which paragraphs a gate enforces whole is the owner's choice, made from a list a session prepares, because the text is the owner's: a session never prunes on its own reading.
rules.says: The owner chooses which paragraphs a gate enforces whole, from a list a session prepares, and a session never prunes or replaces a doctrine paragraph on its own reading.

rules.heading: (plan rules, after rule 15)
rules.quote: *Enforced by:* `session-guards.test.mjs`, which fails when a line of this kind names a file the hub does not have
rules.says: A line replacing a paragraph must name a gate file that exists in the hub, so a replacement cannot point at a gate that is not there.

rules.heading: The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: These paragraphs state what the redesign plan built, one for each behaviour, from its Design parts. Each ends in the gate that holds it where one does.
rules.says: The paragraphs of this section state what the redesign plan built, one paragraph for each behaviour, and each ends in the gate that holds it where one does.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The program and its states.** `PROGRAM.md` holds the family's thesis and the ranked list of every item of work across the hub and the apps.
rules.says: PROGRAM.md holds the family's thesis and the ranked list of every item of work across the hub and the apps, and an entry has a key, a repository, a goal, a state, the plan that carries it, its acceptance and its dependencies.
rules.live_quote: the ranked list of every item of work across the hub and the apps, with each item's goal, acceptance, dependencies, state and plan
rules.missing: The family's thesis, and an entry's key and repository.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: The states are open, planned, running, parked, done and ejected.
rules.says: A program item's state is one of open, planned, running, parked, done or ejected.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: Every plan serves one item and quotes its acceptance, new work enters by being ranked, and a plan's close writes the item's state and what changed.
rules.says: Every plan serves one program item and quotes its acceptance, new work enters only by being ranked in the program, and a plan's close writes the item's state and what changed.
rules.live_quote: a plan serves one item and its close writes the item's state.
rules.missing: That a plan quotes its acceptance, that new work enters only by being ranked, and that the close writes what changed.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: No count of lines or characters gates a plan or shortens one. *Held by:* nothing; the plan's reading of the file is the manager's.
rules.says: No count of lines or characters gates a plan or shortens it, and the manager reads the program file for the plan with no gate holding it.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The wall line.** Before a step goes, at every stop inside it and at a plan's close, one written sentence answers whether the step still serves the item's acceptance
rules.says: Before a step goes, at every stop inside it and at a plan's close, one written sentence must answer whether the step still serves the item's acceptance, whether the item still serves the thesis, and whether what was just seen moved either; it stands in each agent's report after the verdict word and in the review's hand-back, and a no is an eject.
rules.enforcer: none; carried by the agent rules at version 6 and aim-review.md

rules.heading: The wall line
rules.quote: *Held by:* no gate; a gate that judged the sentence would be the kind of gate Design part 9 replaces. The agent rules at version 6 and `aim-review.md` carry the rule.
rules.says: No gate judges the wall-line sentence; the rule is carried by the agent rules at version 6 and by aim-review.md.
rules.enforcer: agent rules version 6 and aim-review.md (no gate)

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The three ejects.** A step ejects to the plan: it hands back EJECT with what it saw and the files it names, and writes nothing after.
rules.says: A step that ejects hands back EJECT with what it saw and the files it names to the plan, and writes nothing after.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: A plan ejects to the program: it closes unfinished, its item returns as ejected with the finding attached and is re-ranked, and the next item is taken.
rules.says: A plan that ejects to the program closes unfinished, its item returns as ejected with the finding attached and is re-ranked, and the next item is taken.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: The program ejects to the owner only for a choice that is the owner's, and that item is parked.
rules.says: The program ejects to the owner only for a choice that is the owner's, and that item is parked.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: A manager note opening with the word Eject closes the pointer only when it names the plan in force by its file name, so a stale line cannot close a later plan's pointer.
rules.says: A manager note opening with the word Eject closes the plan pointer only when it names the plan in force by its file name, and EJECT is read as a state of its own in the pointer, the status and the page.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The step as a list that cannot be done wrong.** Every step carries Facts, Do, Observe and Kill.
rules.says: Every step of a plan carries the four labelled parts Facts, Do, Observe and Kill.
rules.enforcer: plan-guard.mjs (refuses a plan whose step lacks a label, with no latch)

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: An agent repairs its own red check once, in a file it wrote in that send, and a second red check ends the step with nothing written after it
rules.says: An agent may repair its own red check once, in a file it wrote in that send; a second red check ends the step with nothing written after it, and an observation the step did not name ends it as EJECT.
rules.enforcer: plan-guard.mjs; reply-guard.mjs already passes the run after the repair

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: The rule that let a failed command run again after any write is replaced at version 6 by that one repair
rules.says: The old rule that let a failed command run again after any write is replaced, at agent rules version 6, by the single repair of the agent's own red check.

rules.heading: The step as a list that cannot be done wrong
rules.quote: and the code in `reply-guard.mjs` already passes the run after it.
rules.says: The code in reply-guard.mjs already passes the run that follows an agent's single repair of its own red check.

rules.heading: The step as a list that cannot be done wrong
rules.quote: *Held by:* `plan-guard.mjs`, which refuses a plan whose step lacks a label, with no latch.
rules.says: A plan is refused when any of its steps lacks one of the labels Facts, Do, Observe or Kill, and the refusal has no latch.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **Conversation as the default.** Outside an approved plan and outside plan mode a message gets an answer from the files, under the never-rules alone
rules.says: Outside an approved plan and outside plan mode a message gets an answer from the files, under the never-rules alone: no repository write outside a plan, only staging and main reach a remote, and nothing personal lands in a repository.
rules.live_quote: - Only staging and main reach a remote.
rules.missing: That outside an approved plan and plan mode a message gets an answer from the files, and that no repository write happens outside a plan (owner-not-named rule at page.md:30 covers the personal part).

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: Work begins only at the owner's button.
rules.says: Work begins only at the owner's button.
rules.live_quote: - Approval is only the button. A typed word approves nothing.
rules.missing: That no work begins before the button; live text states what counts as approval, not that work waits for it.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: Inside a plan a correction holds sends until it is answered, and the word stop holds agents, sends and repository writes
rules.says: Inside a plan a correction holds sends until it is answered, and the word stop holds agents, sends and repository writes while still passing reading, answering, the status, the plan file, the manager notes and the plan check.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: Sends of agents and workflows stay judged in every state.
rules.says: Sends of agents and workflows stay judged in every state; outside a plan the manager fence and the holds are skipped but the approved-plan, push, Drive, keep-information and pending-message guards keep running, and stop-guard refuses on reply prose under an approved plan only while keeping four refusals always on.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The doctrine read by the part that applies.** The never-rules are on one page, `doctrine/never.md`, read whole at every start and after a compaction;
rules.says: The never-rules (doctrine/never.md) are read whole at every start and after a compaction, the plan rules (doctrine/plans.md) are read whole at the entry to plan mode, agents read the agent rules, and the apps sections (doctrine/apps.md) are read when an item points at them, with DOCTRINE.md as the index.
rules.live_quote: The never-rules are on one short page, `doctrine/never.md`,
rules.missing: That the never-rules are read whole at every start and after a compaction, that plan rules are read whole at plan-mode entry (they now sit in archive/), and that agents read the agent rules; only the apps part and the index role are stated.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The configuration baseline.** `CONFIG.md` lists every configuration item with its state and the program item that may change it;
rules.says: CONFIG.md lists every configuration item with its state and the program item that may change it; a change to any configuration is a program item, a drift found is a finding that becomes one, an open dependency update is an item, and the comparison is done by hand.
rules.enforcer: ConfigChange record of hook-dispatch.mjs (holds a change made in a container)

rules.heading: The configuration baseline
rules.quote: *Held by:* the ConfigChange record of `hook-dispatch.mjs`, which holds a change made in a container; the comparison stays by hand.
rules.says: A configuration change made in a container is held by the ConfigChange record of hook-dispatch.mjs.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **One file for each finding, and several sessions on one hub.** A finding is its own file in `found/`, keyed `Q-HUB-N`
rules.says: Each finding is its own file in found/, keyed Q-HUB-N, so two sessions never edit one file, and the closing check and the plan check take keys from that folder where it exists.
rules.enforcer: foundQueue in hook-dispatch.mjs, read by plan-guard.mjs and stop-guard.mjs

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: A finding's file may end with one line of four kinds, told by its opening words: Put right already, Fix in, Not the repository's, or Not placed, each with a colon.
rules.says: A finding's file may end with one line opening with Put right already, Fix in, Not the repository's, or Not placed (each followed by a colon); the seed reads the last such line, Fix in groups the finding by the files it names, Put right already and Not the repository's leave it out of every batch, and Not placed or no line and no file named gives it no step and lists its key as not placed.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: A landing step ends each finding it files with one.
rules.says: A landing step ends each finding it files with one of the four ending lines.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: The program is appended per app with a pull before every write and an eject on conflict, which the redesign plan did not build
rules.says: The program is appended per app with a pull before every write and an eject on conflict (stated as not built by the redesign plan).

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: a newer hub is taken up at a startup or a resume and never in the middle of a plan: with no plan of the session open the dispatcher brings the gates' copy
rules.says: A newer hub is taken up only at a startup or a resume and never in the middle of a plan: with no plan of the session open the dispatcher fast-forwards the gates' copy and each clean checkout on main and prints a line for each.
rules.live_quote: At every start and resume the hub's copy in the container is brought forward from the hub's main, with the short page, the roles, the procedures, the push guard and the dispatcher.
rules.missing: That it is never done mid-plan, that each clean checkout on main is also fast-forwarded, and that a line is printed for each.

rules.heading: ### The structures of the redesign plan of 2 November 2026
rules.quote: **The measure.** At each plan's close `session-cost.mjs` prints tokens by tier, the owner's messages, go-words, corrections, refusals and agents
rules.says: At each plan's close session-cost.mjs is run to print tokens by tier, the owner's messages, go-words, corrections, refusals and agents, and the manager writes the close entry under P-10 in PROGRAM.md so a plan is judged against the plans before it.

rules.heading: ## 0g. Act from the owner's goal and the record, and verify once.
rules.quote: Every action is checked against what the owner is trying to achieve and against what the record already settles, before it is taken.
rules.says: Every action is checked, before it is taken, against what the owner is trying to achieve and against what the record already settles.

rules.heading: ## 0g. Act from the owner's goal and the record, and verify once.
rules.quote: The owner's work is developing the apps: each repo's ranked roadmap names the next work, and a session works it in parallel across the horizon
rules.says: The owner's work is developing the apps; each repo's ranked roadmap names the next work, and a session works it in parallel across the horizon, never polishing one item for hours while the rest wait, and speed comes from cutting what is unnecessary.

rules.heading: ## 0g. Act from the owner's goal and the record, and verify once.
rules.quote: Verification is not that: it runs once, over the integrated release at the promotion to main, which is the public boundary, and never per step.
rules.says: Verification runs once, over the integrated release at the promotion to main (the public boundary), and never per step; staging carries the owner's own pass on the device and the app's test page as the measurement, and nothing walks it.
rules.enforcer: stop-guard.mjs (refuses a reply offering to drop verification to save time)

rules.heading: ## 0g. Act from the owner's goal and the record, and verify once.
rules.quote: `stop-guard.mjs` refuses a reply that asks the owner for the next work
rules.says: A reply never asks the owner for the next work.

rules.heading: 0g. Act from the owner's goal and the record, and verify once
rules.quote: and one that offers to drop verification to save time.
rules.says: A reply never offers to drop verification to save time.

rules.heading: ### Every time is California time
rules.quote: Every time given to the owner is converted to California local time (America/Los_Angeles).
rules.says: Every time given to the owner is converted to California local time (America/Los_Angeles), and report.mjs converts the status stamp.
rules.live_quote: - Every time given to the owner is California time.

rules.heading: ### The slots — structural habits that look like content and are not
rules.quote: A reply here has recurring shapes that get FILLED rather than earned.
rules.says: Recurring reply shapes that get filled rather than earned read as substance and cost the reader, so they are named in the list below so they can be refused.

rules.heading: ### The slots — structural habits that look like content and are not
rules.quote: - **The closing reflection.** Ruled on in §12: it goes in a file or it does not get said.
rules.says: A reply carries no closing reflection: it goes in a file or it is not said (ruled on in section 12), and it is the generator of most of the other slots.
